lesson.text: A linear model describes a steady change: a start value plus a rate times time. A plant 5 cm tall growing 2 cm a week: h = 2w + 5.
The rate of change is the slope; the start (initial value) is the y-intercept.
From two readings: (3 weeks, 11 cm) and (7 weeks, 19 cm) give the rate (19 − 11) ÷ (7 − 3) = 2 cm a week.
Graphs tell stories: a flat part means no change; steeper means faster.

exercises.prompt: A pool holds 100 L and fills at 20 L a minute. How much after 6 minutes, in litres?
In h = 2w + 5, what is the starting height?
A flat part of a distance-time graph means the object stopped.
A gym charges 10 coins to join and 3 coins a visit. Which function gives the cost c for v visits?
A candle is 20 cm tall and burns 2 cm an hour. How tall after 7 hours, in cm?
Which part of a graph shows the fastest change?
A tank holds 30 L after 2 minutes and 50 L after 6 minutes. How many litres a minute?
A tank holds 30 L after 2 minutes, filling at 5 L a minute. How much did it hold at the start, in litres?
